cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code directly concatenates user input from params[:config] into command arguments without any sanitization or escaping, which is the exact mechanism of CWE-77 Command Injection.

connection.evidence: User input from params[:config] flows directly to arg_list, which becomes part of a system command executed via run_cmd(). The connection path is: params[:config] -> option/value -> arg_list -> run_cmd()

diff_causality.evidence: If this line were reverted, the config options would not be added to arg_list, and thus would not be passed to the system command, eliminating the injection vector.

security_control.evidence: There is no input sanitization or escaping of option or value before concatenation into the command argument.
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-77 requires that special elements in command arguments be neutralized to prevent command injection.
existing_controls_checked: No input validation or sanitization of params[:config] values
No escaping of option or value strings before command construction
security_control.deficiency_evidence: The code directly interpolates user input into a shell command argument without any neutralization, making it vulnerable to injection.

concrete_impact.evidence: If an attacker controls the config parameter and provides malicious values with special shell characters (like ';', '&', '|', '`', '$()'), they can inject arbitrary commands that will execute on the system with the privileges of the executing user.

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the configuration options from params[:config] would not be added to arg_list, and therefore would not be passed as arguments to the system command. This would eliminate the command injection vulnerability because no user-controlled values would be interpolated into the command string.
supporting_evidence: params[:config] is directly iterated over in line 2324
User input from params[:config] flows directly to option and value variables
The option=value string is directly appended to arg_list without sanitization
arg_list is passed as command arguments to run_cmd() on line 2331
review_comment: User input from params[:config] flows directly into command arguments without sanitization. An attacker could inject shell metacharacters to execute arbitrary commands. The fix is to escape or validate all option and value fields before concatenating them into the command argument.
